lines: The link between Rack and a Haken Eagan Matrix instrument: it holds the MIDI connection, scans the presets, and carries the surface out as control voltage; other CHEM modules work through one
Sets the master level on the instrument, which is attenuation on Haken instruments and post level on an Osmose
Counts up one per second to a maximum of 60 minutes and then wraps to zero; nothing in the module or in the instrument reads it
Sends a short test phrase of MIDI notes to the instrument, so you can hear whether the connection carries sound
Reflects music on MIDI channels 2 and up from that controller down to channels 15 and below, so a second Eagan Matrix surface can be played at the same time without note collisions
Passes only notes and expression from that controller to the instrument, dropping the control messages that would otherwise change the preset
Blocks everything from that controller, which mutes it without unplugging it
Slews the Y output, with no slew fully anticlockwise and the slowest movement fully clockwise
Slews the Z output, with no slew fully anticlockwise and the slowest movement fully clockwise
Lengthens the slew range of the two trim pots beside the Y and Z outputs by a factor of ten
A high gate blocks that controller's MIDI from reaching the instrument and lights the button beside it; the gate reads high at 0.8V and above
Carries 10V while the instrument is able to accept MIDI and make sound, and 0V while it is busy loading a preset, scanning presets or remaking Mahling data
Carries 10V on a channel while a note is held on that channel of the playing surface, and 0V when the note ends
The pitch of the note held on that channel, as a volt per octave with the surface's pitch bend folded in; 0V is MIDI note 60
The front-to-back position on that channel, 0-10V, taken from whichever continuous controller the instrument has assigned to Y
The pressure on that channel, 0-10V, taken from whichever continuous controller the instrument has assigned to Z
Note — a module added to a patch finds the first Eagan Matrix instrument connected to the computer and connects to it; if there is more than one, click the HAKEN button to choose
Note — MIDI usually stays silent unless the patch also holds one of the VCV Audio modules with a driver chosen, so add an Audio module before this one
Note — the Preset and Play modules show nothing until the presets have been scanned into a database, which is started from the Presets submenu of the Core actions menu on this panel
Note — the C1 and c2 buttons choose MIDI controllers whose data is passed on to the instrument; the MIDI Reset button above HAKEN restarts the connection, and control-clicking it clears every one
Note — to control a second Eagan Matrix instrument, add a second one of these to the patch
Menu — Presets — on the Core actions menu reached from the hamburger button, not the right-click menu; scans the instrument to build the preset databases Preset and Play read
Menu — Log MIDI — on the Core actions menu; writes every MIDI message sent and received into a log file in the pachde-CHEM folder under your Rack user folder
Menu — Disconnect MIDI — on the Core actions menu; drops the MIDI connection to the instrument until it is turned off again
Menu — Zero XYZ on Note off — on the Core actions menu; drops the X, Y and Z voltage for a channel to zero when the note ends, in place of holding the last value
Menu — MPE channels (2-15) only — on the Core actions menu; makes the W, X, Y and Z outputs 14 channels taken from MIDI channels 2 to 15, in place of 16 channels taken from every MIDI channel
Menu — Silence WYXZ — on the Core actions menu; clears the stored note, bend, front-to-back and pressure for every channel, so the four surface outputs fall to 0V
Menu — Haken Requests — on the Core actions menu; sends single requests from the Haken MIDI protocol to the instrument, for working out what has gone wrong

chem-jack.notes: The four min and max trim pots are read from the instrument in Jack.cpp:90-93 and are absent from process_params at Jack.cpp:112-128, which sends only the two assignments, the shift, the shift action and the keep flag; no other code in the plugin writes ccMin1, ccMax1, ccMin2 or ccMax2. So the four knobs are indicators in 2.0.3, not controls, and the module documentation at doc/jack.md describing them as choosing the minimum and maximum is wrong for this version. The maker also names both jack 2 knobs "Jack 1 minimum" and "Jack 1 maximum" in Jack.cpp:23-24, a copy-and-paste slip that leaves the jack 2 pots wearing the jack 1 tooltips.

lines: The Eagan Matrix settings the other CHEM modules leave out: surface direction, transposition, the X, Y and Z assignments, polyphony, note processing, mono mode, tuning, rounding and MIDI routing
Reverses the direction of the playing surface
Sets the MIDI note number at the centre of the touch area, from 16 to 108; a setting of 16 or below means no touch area at all, and right-clicking lets you type the number
Transposes the surface by setting the MIDI note number that sounds at the frequency of middle C; right-clicking lets you type the number
Chooses the bend range for X, the last entry combining MPE at 96 on channels 2 and up with a chosen range on channel 1
Chooses the continuous controller the front-to-back axis is sent on
Chooses the continuous controller pressure is sent on
Chooses how notes are produced: Static velocity (127), Dynamic velocity, Formula velocity, No Notes, Ethervox, or Kyma
Chooses which note wins when notes collide: oldest channel, same pitch, lowest channel, highest channel, or the highest two, three or four channels
Sets the number of voices the instrument plays at once, from none to eight
Doubles the number of voices by halving the computation spent on each
Doubles the rate the matrix is computed at
Detunes the whole instrument in cents either side of centre
Sets how hard the surface has to be pressed before a note starts
Sets the level of the instrument's audio input
Turns mono mode on, so the surface plays one note at a time
Chooses how one note moves to the next in mono mode: weighted portamento, legato or retrigger on high pressure, legato or retrigger on touch or on touch and lift, and three of those at full pressure
Sets the interval from the first note beyond which mono behaviour starts, from a semitone to three octaves, or off for the whole surface
Chooses when rounding is applied: Normal, Release, Y, or Reverse Y
Rounds the first note of a phrase to the scale as well as the ones after it
Sets how fast a rounded note slides to its pitch, from none to fastest
Chooses the tuning of the surface: an equal temperament of a chosen number of steps, a whole-number-ratio tuning for a chosen scale, or a table made with the Pitch Table Editor
Turns off MIDI arriving at the instrument from reaching that destination, where the destinations across the row are the sound engine, the control voltage converter, and the instrument's MIDI output
Turns off the playing surface from reaching that destination, where the destinations across the row are the sound engine, the control voltage converter, and the instrument's MIDI output
Turns on the instrument's Preserve MIDI setting, which keeps the MIDI settings made here when a preset is loaded
Turns on the instrument's Preserve Surface setting, which keeps the surface settings made here when a preset is loaded
Sets how far the voltage at the RATE input moves the round rate, from -100% to 100%, a negative amount inverting the voltage
A high gate turns rounding of the first note on and a low gate turns it off, reading high above 9.5V and low below 0.125V; while a cable is patched the button on the panel no longer sets it
Moves the round rate away from its slider position, bipolar, scaled by the modulation amount knob and clamped to 0-10V
Note — nothing reaches the instrument until the module is linked to a CHEM Core; putting it beside a linked CHEM module links it, or click the link button at the bottom of the panel to pick a Core
Note — the AES3 button above the input jacks opens a menu for the instrument's digital audio input, offering 48k, 96k and Sync to incoming, and reading back the rate it detects
Note — the equivalent of the instrument's Preserve Pedals setting is on CHEM Jack, not here
Menu — Zero modulation — sets the modulation amount for the RATE input to zero

lines: The preset browser for the Eagan Matrix instrument: search, filter by category and attribute, and load User or System presets; it works through a CHEM Core
Scans through the preset list one entry at a time, the same movement the up and down arrow keys give; control-shift-drag moves it finely, and clicking it loads the preset at the cursor
Loads the preset at the cursor on the instrument
Stops the MIDI keyboard chosen for navigation from moving the cursor, so it can be played without changing the selection
Note — the list stays empty until the presets have been scanned into a database, which is started from the Presets submenu of the Core actions menu on CHEM Core and takes up to an hour
Note — nothing reaches the instrument until the module is linked to a CHEM Core; putting it beside a linked CHEM module links it, or click the link button at the bottom of the panel to pick a Core
Note — type in the search box at the top and press ENTER to narrow the list, which matches preset names and the raw metadata codes; ESC clears the text, and TAB moves between the box and the list
Note — the search options hamburger beside the box picks whether names, metadata or both are searched, whether a match must fall at a word start, and whether the list updates on ENTER
Note — metadata is searched as two-letter codes rather than words, so CL finds the Classic category and EP the electric pianos
Note — the filter buttons narrow the list by Category, Type, Character, Matrix component and Setting; control-clicking one entry chooses that one alone, and a red lamp shows a filter is active
Note — the preset actions hamburger sorts the list alphabetically, by category or by preset number, scrolls the playing preset into view or follows it, and keeps filters across sessions
Note — the MIDI navigation button beside the knob picks a MIDI keyboard or controller and opens a dialog where each action is taught by MIDI learn: click between the brackets, then press a key
Names the overlay preset a patch is built around, and passes it to the CHEM Extended Macro modules beside it so their macros are sent only while that preset is playing
Note — it does nothing until a preset is configured, which is done from the hamburger menu on the panel
Note — with a preset configured, the chiclet button under the lamp loads it on the instrument, and the green lamp at the top lights while the playing preset matches the configured one
Menu — Use live preset — on the hamburger menu on the panel, not the right-click menu; makes the preset the instrument is playing the one this module tracks
Note — one of these belongs to one CHEM Core, and each Extended Macro module links to the Overlay on its left, or through a run of adjacent Extended Macro modules to a common one
Note — the hamburger menu on the panel also sets a title for the module and the colours of the panel and the title text
Note — extended macros are numbered 7 to 90 and exist only in overlay presets; the Eagan Matrix Overlay Developer's Guide, shipped with the Haken firmware, is what describes making them
chem-overlay.notes: The module has no parameters, inputs or outputs at all. doc/overlay.md says Use live preset is in the module's right-click menu; in the code it is on the panel hamburger widget (XM-Overlay/Overlay-ui.cpp:11-59), and OverlayUi::appendContextMenu adds nothing beyond the shared theme items.

lines: Up to eight knobs for the extended macros of an overlay preset, each one configured by hand for a macro number, a name, a range and a control mode; it works with a CHEM Overlay
Note — a new module is blank and has no controls at all until it is configured: put it beside its CHEM Overlay, then press F2 or choose Edit from the right-click menu to open the editing panel
Note — in the editing panel, click a knob number to work on that slot, then give it a name, a macro number from 7 to 90, a range and a control mode; Load preset macros fills the macro menu
Note — the three control modes are Knob only, a knob with no jack; CV-modulated, a knob with a jack and a modulation amount; and CV-driven, a jack with a moving track in place of a knob
Note — the knobs and jacks are built when the module is configured, so none of them can be clicked for help here; the maker's own tooltip on each carries the name you gave it
Note — control voltage into these jacks is read as bipolar, -5V to 5V, so an LFO feeding one should have its offset turned off
Note — to control more than eight extended macros, add another one of these
Note — MIDI to the instrument stops while the editing panel is open
Menu — Edit — opens and closes the editing panel to the right, and is greyed out until the module has found an Overlay
Menu — Center knobs — sets every configured macro knob to the middle of its range
chem-xm.notes: Every parameter and input on this module is created at run time from the user's configuration, so none of them appears in the census with a widget position and none can be reached by a click. The eight knobs, the modulation amount, the range minimum and maximum, and the eight jacks are all in that group.

lines: Sixteen pads, each holding a MIDI phrase you write out yourself, for sending Eagan Matrix commands that no other CHEM module covers; it works through a CHEM Core
A rising edge sends the MIDI phrase held by the pad of the same name; it reads high above 0.5V and low below 0.1V, and an undefined pad sends nothing
Note — every pad starts empty and sends nothing until you write its MIDI: click the e button to open the editing panel, click a pad, and type its definition
Note — definitions are written in the maker's Haken Control Language, which covers channel, control code, macro, program change, data streams and the matrix, formula, graph and convolution pokes
Note — a definition that opens with a comment in double quotes uses that comment as the pad's tooltip
Note — press control-enter or click the compile button to check a definition; a pad whose definition failed shows a red lamp and carries the error in its tooltip
Note — the send button in the editing panel fires the phrase so you can hear what it does before leaving the panel
Note — values are not range-checked before they are sent, and a wrong one can leave the instrument silent or showing an internal error until the preset is reloaded or the instrument is restarted
Note — the pads are drawn as one widget rather than as sixteen parameters, so a pad cannot be clicked for help; only its trigger jack can
Note — nothing reaches the instrument until the module is linked to a CHEM Core; putting it beside a linked CHEM module links it, or click the link button at the bottom of the panel to pick a Core
